title: A card statement paid by a parent (a repay with no paying account) and a travel spend on the home card posted late (final_review_2 S10 and S6, the Q watch items; both were sound)
story: Set up Mon 4 Jan 2027: the bank holds 300,000. A card closes on the 15th and is paid on the 10th of the next month (moved later) from the bank; its last statement (15 Dec) was 0 and nothing is on it. On Fri 8 Jan 40,000 is spent on the card. A parent pays that statement straight to the card company on Tue 9 Feb: the person records a payment to the card from no account of theirs. On Fri 5 Feb, travelling, a dinner of 80.00 USD goes on the yen card; the person types it as about 12,000 yen (rough). The card posts it on Wed 17 Feb, 8 working days later, as 12,830 yen (the rate and a 2% fee, 6.9% more); the statement is read on Sat 20 Feb. Every amount is made up.

events.note: the dinner as the card posted it
paid by a parent: no paying account

asks.question: bank_today
asks.why: 300,000 (opening) - 0 (the card statement was paid by a parent: a repay with no paying account takes nothing from the bank) = 300,000

asks.question: owed_now
asks.why: 40,000 (Fri 8 Jan) - 40,000 (paid by a parent, Tue 9 Feb) + 12,000 (dinner, Fri 5 Feb, typed roughly) = 12,000

asks.question: not_seen_yet
asks.note: The statement's payment c@2027-02-10 is settled by the parent's payment, so nothing is waited for.

asks.question: owed_now
asks.why: 40,000 (Fri 8 Jan) - 40,000 (paid by a parent) + 12,830 (the dinner as posted Wed 17 Feb; it replaces the rough 12,000, within 10%, matched by its buy date) = 12,830
asks.note: Posted 8 working days after the buy, outside the card's 7 working days by its posted date; its buy date is the typed day, so it matches [L matching q4].

asks.question: card_due
asks.why: 12,830 (the dinner, posted Wed 17 Feb, after the 15 Feb close, so in the statement closing 15 Mar) = 12,830
asks.note: The 15 Feb statement holds nothing new, so no payment is due on 10 Mar; the open one is paid on Sat 10 Apr, moved later to Mon 12 Apr.
